messages.subject: Possible to select all species (17) and only draw one study region for all?
messages.subject_clean: Possible to select all species (17) and only draw one study region for all?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am having an issue drawing one study region for all 17 species in the map I am creating for bat species present in a National Forest.
I get to the step "Process Envs", "Draw Study Region", I draw the polygon around the National Forest but that polygon is only attributed to the first species in my Species menu, not to all seventeen in the study.

How do I apply the drawn polygon to all of the species at once? I have tried to draw multiple polygons but that does not seem to be an option.

Thanks in advance for any help!

messages.subject: Re: Possible to select all species (17) and only draw one study region for all?
messages.subject_clean: Possible to select all species (17) and only draw one study region for all?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
To accomplish this, you just need to check off the "Batch" box at the bottom of the module. This will run the step of analysis for ALL the species you have uploaded.

messages.subject_clean: Error in loading the user specified variables
messages.body_plain:
You can try doing this in R: use the terra::mask() function with the is.na <http://is.na>() function to find and replace NA values within your rasters.

This error message occurs because some downstream analyses will not work if there are nonuniform NA values within the env data.

messages.subject: Re: Urgent Help!!
messages.body_plain:
You can try doing this in R: use the terra::mask() function with the is.na <http://is.na>() function to find and replace NA values within your rasters.

In regard to the WorldClim data, occurrence records are removed if they are duplicates or when they fall within the same environmental grid cell. To include all points, increase grid cell resolution to 30 arcsec. If points are still removed, try Maxent outside of Wallace, which allows this option to be turned off, but caution that this may cause bias to these variables.
